Anonymous ICE agent blames hiring surge and training cuts for shootings

tags: immigration, policing, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

An anonymous veteran Homeland Security Investigations agent said in a published interview that HSI personnel are furious over recent shootings by ICE's Enforcement and Removal Operations branch, attributing them to poor vetting, cut training and new, less restrictive enforcement mandates. The agent said an ERO officer who shot and killed a man with his child in the car in Maine in July was a surge hire with a history of domestic violence who would not have passed a standard background investigation. Asked about a New York City shooting in which officers fired at a vehicle carrying a child, the agent said blame lay with the officers and that there were many alternative ways to arrest the target, Oscar Belgal, a 28-year-old Dominican national with prior convictions. The agent rejected Mayor Mamdani's call to abolish ICE and said the city should have transferred Belgal to immigration custody after his earlier prison term.

Guilfoyle accused of seeking $100,000 from GOP donor before confirmation hearing

tags: politics, legal
sources: @groundnews

U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle allegedly asked a Republican donor to pay off $100,000 in credit card debt in exchange for access to the Trump administration, according to the Wall Street Journal. Text messages reviewed by CBS News indicate Guilfoyle told businessman Eric Deters that wiring the money to her American Express account would keep the payment from appearing publicly; the request came six days before her July 2025 Senate confirmation hearing. Deters said he never sent the money, called the arrangement a quid pro quo, and said he had previously paid Guilfoyle $300,000 for appearances, Donald Trump Jr. $200,000 and Eric Trump $100,000. Guilfoyle's attorney questioned the messages' authenticity, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Vice President JD Vance said they did not know the details.

Monitored wildlife populations fell 73% between 1970 and 2022

tags: climate, environment
sources: @groundnews

Wildlife populations monitored worldwide declined by an average of 73% between 1970 and 2022, according to the World Wide Fund for Nature's 2026 Living Planet Report, which tracked 35,803 populations across 5,790 species. Freshwater populations saw the largest average decline at 85%, followed by land species at 69% and marine species at 59%, with South America recording a 95% drop and Africa 80%. Habitat destruction was the most reported threat, alongside climate change, pollution and overexploitation. Researchers cautioned that the figure reflects average population declines rather than the share of individual animals lost.

Louisiana police chief candidate faces child rape charges and runs unopposed

tags: politics, legal, policing
sources: @aaronparnas

Christopher Paul, a Republican candidate for city police chief in Elizabeth, Louisiana, is running unopposed after the only other candidate withdrew, according to the Guardian. He currently faces two counts of second-degree rape relating to allegations involving two 13-year-old girls about 20 years ago, with a complaint filed in August of this year. Some residents have said the position should be changed from an elected one to an appointed one.

Trump administration begins removing more than 500 trees in Washington DC

tags: environment, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The Trump administration has begun cutting down upwards of 500 trees at the East Potomac Golf Course in Washington, D.C., according to the Washington Post. The National Park Service says the removals are part of an effort to restore the site, but residents and observers on the ground describe the trees as healthy, including mature oaks and maples, and have reacted with anger.

Trump demands eight Nobel Peace Prizes as supporters target SNL

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

President Trump is demanding eight Nobel Peace Prizes, one for each of the wars he claims to have ended, after this year's prize was awarded to someone else. For the second consecutive week, Trump supporters have called for Saturday Night Live to be cancelled over sketches mocking the president's reaction to not winning the prize. Trump also said he may rename the Atlantic or Pacific Ocean the "Trump Ocean".
